A network graph shows **relationships**: nodes connected by edges, laid out so that connected
things sit near each other. The usual R reach is `igraph` or `networkD3`, but here we build one with
[canvasXpress](https://canvasxpress.org) — draggable, hover-labelled, force-directed, and
**reproducible**, because the whole figure is one portable `data` + `config` spec.

## The data shape

canvasXpress builds a network from two tables: **nodes** (`id`, `name`, `group`) and **edges**
(`id1`, `id2`, `value`). Swap this simulated three-community graph for your own.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(canvasXpress)

set.seed(1)
grp   <- rep(c("Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma"), each = 7)
ids   <- paste0("n", seq_along(grp))
nodes <- data.frame(id = ids, name = paste0(grp, ave(grp, grp, FUN = seq_along)),
                    group = grp, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Dense within a community, sparse between communities — the structure a layout reveals.
e1 <- c(); e2 <- c(); ev <- c()
for (g in unique(grp)) {
  m <- ids[grp == g]
  for (i in seq_along(m)) for (j in seq_along(m))
    if (i < j && runif(1) < 0.5) { e1 <- c(e1, m[i]); e2 <- c(e2, m[j]); ev <- c(ev, sample(1:5, 1)) }
}
for (k in 1:6) {                                     # a few cross-community links
  pair <- sample(unique(grp), 2)
  e1 <- c(e1, sample(ids[grp == pair[1]], 1)); e2 <- c(e2, sample(ids[grp == pair[2]], 1)); ev <- c(ev, 1)
}
edges <- data.frame(id1 = e1, id2 = e2, value = ev, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

## The plot

Pass the two tables as `nodeData` and `edgeData`; `colorNodeBy` colours by the community, and
`networkLayoutType = "forceDirected"` runs the physics simulation.

```{r}
canvasXpress(
  nodeData          = nodes,
  edgeData          = edges,
  graphType         = "Network",
  networkLayoutType = "forceDirected",
  colorNodeBy       = "group",
  nodeSize          = 25,
  showAnimation     = TRUE,
  title             = "A small community network",
  width             = 650,
  height            = 500
)
```

Drag any node and the layout settles around it; hover to read the label. The three communities
separate on their own because within-group edges outnumber the cross-group ones.

## Why "reproducible"

The nodes, edges and `config` **are** the figure — one portable specification. The same spec renders
the identical network from Python or JavaScript, and can be validated and re-rendered later.
